proposals.title: Let an India-only channel tell India topics without the global/local quota
proposals.change: generator/reach.py applies the English channels' rule to every channel: at most 1 local Short a day and 4 local in the last 11, and a global video must be in USD. India Maps (Hindi, INR, India's map only) has no global videos by design, so from tomorrow its second daily Short fails check-plan, and after 4 videos every Short does. Give a channel whose audience is one country a pack setting (e.g. channel.json "audience": "IN" / reach mode "home") under which reach.check_plan treats its home-country topics as its 'global' (no USD rule, no local quota, no 1M-views reason) and for_state reports local_allowed true; keep the rule unchanged for every other channel. Add tests in generator/tests/test_reach.py for both cases (tests only grow).
proposals.expectedEffect: India Maps can make its 2 Shorts a day; without it the channel ships 1 a day, then none after its 4th video.
proposals.risk: Must not loosen the rule for the English channels: scope it to the channel setting.
proposals.reason: already on main: channel.json homeCountry IN and generator/reach.py skip the quota and USD rule for a one-country channel (owner, 2026-11-25)

proposals.title: Kerala is officially Keralam since August 2026: update the map label
proposals.change: The Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill 2026 passed Lok Sabha 11 Aug and Rajya Sabha 12 Aug 2026 and got the President's assent 18 Aug 2026. remotion/src/flat/data/india.json still labels it name 'Kerala', hi 'केरल'. In scripts/build_india_map.py set the display names to 'Keralam' / 'केरलम' (keep 'Kerala' as an accepted alias so old videos and the topic feed's items still resolve), regenerate india.json, and teach the writer prompt/recipe to say केरलम for the state today (केरल only for history before 2026).
proposals.expectedEffect: No outdated state name on an India-map channel whose viewers correct the map in comments.
proposals.risk: Old videos re-render with the new label unless the alias keeps them; that is fine.
